solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Star part, so got in cast

indicators.note: to cast is to throw or mould, so these letters are thrown into a new form

explanation.surface: An actor brags that a starring part got them into the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' signals an anagram of PART SO GOT IN; the comma inside the fodder only disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead character of a drama is its star role, the central figure of the story.

clue.text: Income from flat in French street

indicators.note: in places the word for flat inside the French street word

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means flat, level

explanation.surface: Rent earned from an apartment on a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment, but it is the adjective: level, EVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is money coming in, a synonym for income, especially of a state or business.

clue.text: Fair ball or tee shot

indicators.note: shot in the sense of ruined or worn out, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer judges a tee shot fair enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of middling or passable is a synonym of acceptable, good enough.

clue.text: Goblet with Guinness head on bar

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here taken from the stout's name

parts.note: a rail is a bar, as in a towel rail

explanation.surface: A pint glass of Guinness, its frothy head standing on the pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness's 'head' is the foam on a pint in the surface, but here it is just its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail of legend is the cup or goblet used at the Last Supper.

clue.text: One standing in order to sit?

definitions.text: One standing in order to sit?

parts.words: One standing in order to sit?
parts.note: a candidate stands for election hoping to sit as a member of parliament, so standing leads to sitting

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone on their feet precisely so they can sit down.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a candidate 'stands' for election and an elected MP 'sits' in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A person put forward as a candidate for office is said to stand for election.

clue.text: A necessity when raising fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue raising lifts the run upward, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a must is a necessity
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: Lifting a crop of fruit is essential work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' turns the whole run A MUST AS upwards, giving SATSUMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small loose-skinned citrus fruit, a kind of mandarin.

clue.text: Mob supporting rope catching case of embezzlement

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: catching means the rope word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a lariat is a lasso, a rope

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: A crowd backs hanging a fraudster caught embezzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' and 'case of' both point inward: the rope holds the edges of embezzlement just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The proletariat is the working class, disparagingly the mob or masses.

clue.text: Rogue state creates damage

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous rascal, a rogue
to air a view is to state it

explanation.surface: A rogue nation wreaks destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue state' reads as a political phrase; it splits into a noun and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to weaken or damage it.

clue.text: Second vehicle's first in concrete discharge

indicators.note: in places the second and vehicle pieces inside the concrete word

parts.note: concrete as an adjective means real, actual
a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word vehicle

explanation.surface: A second vehicle is first to tip out a load of concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concrete' is the building material in the surface but the adjective REAL in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Discharge in the sense of dismissal from post matches the removal of someone from office.

clue.text: Owns openings around top of mine

indicators.note: around means the openings word wraps round the letter from mine

parts.note: adits are horizontal entrances to mines

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mining company owns the openings to the pit's top.
explanation.walkthrough: An ADIT is a horizontal passage into a mine, apt for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up to something is to admit it, so owns and admits are synonyms in the confessional sense.

clue.text: After gym, ran about getting disjointed

indicators.note: about signals that these letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone went for a run after the gym and became incoherent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AFTER GYM RAN; 'getting' joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken into bits and lacking connection is disjointed, incomplete.

clue.text: Student's less fat eating recipe

indicators.note: eating means the less-fat word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: leaner means having less fat
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, seen in prescriptions

explanation.surface: A student on a diet consumes a recipe with less fat.
explanation.walkthrough: R for recipe is from the Latin 'recipe', meaning take, at the head of old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone studying a subject, a synonym for a student.

clue.text: Left with irritation say, following inactivity

indicators.note: say indicates the letters are heard as a spoken sound rather than spelt

parts.note: anger is irritation

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross after being left idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes the word for irritation heard rather than spelt; the answer is pronounced LANG-er, so its ending matches ANGER said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is listless sluggishness, a lack of energy or activity.

clue.text: Barrister secretly concealing brief

indicators.note: concealing means the answer is held inside the words barrister secretly

explanation.surface: A lawyer quietly hides a case file from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a barrister's case papers in the surface but is the adjective: short.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief and to the point, using few words.

clue.text: Recoil from blast echoed around rifle end

indicators.note: around means the blast and echoed words wrap round the end letter of rifle

parts.note: a boom is a loud blast
rang means resounded, echoed

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The kick from a rifle shot that rang round the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps the blast and echo pieces round the rifle's last letter, which sits between them; 'Recoil' is the verb, to backfire.
explanation.definitionFit: To boomerang is to recoil on the one responsible, like the curved stick returning.

clue.text: Furthest route changed on flash street

indicators.note: changed means the letters of route are put in a different order

parts.note: a flash is an instant, a mo

explanation.surface: A diversion sends traffic down a flashy street at the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns ROUTE into OUTER; 'flash' is the noun, a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Outermost means farthest from the centre, the most remote.

clue.text: Queen back, ready for show

indicators.note: back means the queen's letters are written in reverse

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
present in the sense of ready, here, as in present and correct

explanation.surface: The Queen returns, prepared for the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, for Elizabeth Regina, reads backwards as RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent is to depict or show, as a painting represents a scene.

clue.text: Intention is almost honourable with model

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the honourable word is left off

parts.note: pure means morally clean, honourable
to pose is to model, as for an artist

explanation.surface: A man's plans are nearly honourable, involving a model.
explanation.walkthrough: PURE loses its last letter to give PUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A purpose is an aim or goal, the thing one intends.

clue.text: Former wife put on pounds, sweetheart's loss

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
pounds are enclosures for animals, also called pens
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, a crossword convention

explanation.surface: An ex-wife gains weight and is mourned by a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pounds' looks like weight or money; it is animal enclosures, PENS. 'sweetheart' is the heart of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is a cost, something paid out, so a loss of money.

clue.text: Silver monkey with mouth open

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
ape is a loose synonym of monkey

explanation.surface: A silverback monkey gapes, jaw dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape describes a person staring open-mouthed in wonder.

clue.text: Jack in for a group playing

parts.note: a band is a musical group
on means playing, as in a show being on

explanation.surface: A jack is drafted into a playing band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack in' is British slang for give up or quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack something in is British slang for giving it up, so abandoning it.

clue.text: Last of malaria through extremities of tsetse fly

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of the word malaria

parts.note: via means by way of, through

indicators.note: the extremities of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Malaria is carried by the tsetse fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' is the insect in the surface but the verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to fly an aircraft, to pilot.

clue.text: Becoming a rugby player, very big

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very big

explanation.surface: A rugby forward grows into a giant.
explanation.walkthrough: OS stands for outsize, a British clothing label for very large garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming in the sense of fitting or appropriate matches apropos, meaning apt or opportune.

clue.text: The female entertainer ends stark…

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A female performer finishes her act starkly.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer and stark both mean utter or absolute, as in sheer folly or stark madness.

clue.text: He's practical about American agenda

parts.note: re means about, concerning
an agenda is a list of items

explanation.surface: A pragmatic man is concerned with the American political agenda.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is a person who faces facts and deals with situations practically.

clue.text: Start of pussy cat's spring

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the ounce is a big cat, the snow leopard

explanation.surface: The opening of a pet cat's leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' is the noun leap; the ounce is another name for the snow leopard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pounce is a sudden spring or leap onto prey.

clue.text: Someone getting on in cold, stertorously?

indicators.note: in means the answer sits within the words cold stertorously

explanation.surface: An elderly person sleeps snoring heavily in the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Stertorous breathing is heavy snoring, which fits the picture of an aged sleeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on is an idiom for growing old, and an oldster is an elderly person.

clue.text: Keen going on about unruly teen

indicators.note: about means the going-on word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: prating means chattering, going on

indicators.note: unruly means the letters of teen are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teenager who won't behave keeps going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' scrambles teen, and 'about' puts that jumble just after the first letter of the chatter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen in the sense of sharp or incisive, as a keen mind, matches penetrating.
